*A shrewd assessor of valuables, you will buy anything, legal or otherwise, and turn it around for a tidy profit.*

*'I know it's hot, you know it's hot, even Sigmar himself knows it's hot. When I ask is it hot, don't insult me by saying no. Luckily for you, I deal in hot, so stop with all the panicking and horseshit.'*

*'So you say you got this from a forgotten orc lair? Course you did. Say no more, eh? Whose land was this lair on? Because that dagger has a Tussen-Hochen crest, if you try selling it, some snitch will tell the watch. Best take them to Luther Nitche and he'll help you offload them, no questions asked.'*

A Fence buys thieves' spoils and sells them, often to buyers unaware the goods are stolen. Some operate as pawnbrokers or importers, using legitimate businesses as a front for their more lucrative trade.

They also act as intermediaries — when high-profile items vanish, interested buyers ask a Fence where they might be found. Some work on commission, connecting clients with thieves who can steal to order. While some build a reputation in one place, others remain constantly on the move, trafficking in portable valuables. After all, a painting stolen in Altdorf is much easier to sell in Talabheim. The most successful build networks of dealers and thieves, moving valuable goods through the black market.

The life of a Fence is risky, so they are always ready to disappear or skip town. Adventuring suits them well, allowing them to make new contacts, gather information about valuable goods, and stay one step ahead of the authorities.

Playing a Fence lets you move comfortably between respectable society and the criminal underworld. You can cultivate valuable contacts, broker illicit deals, and always know someone who can acquire — or dispose of — almost anything.

*Just when you abandoned all hope, your suffering and the righteousness of your god saved you!*
*'We scourge this flesh and spill this blood, for his Empire, in Sigmar's name!'* — Viktorina Schwefel, Flagellant

Flagellants travel the Empire, flogging themselves in penance for their own sins and the sins of others. The vast majority are devout followers of Sigmar, though a rare few dedicate themselves to other gods. Whatever their creed, all believe the End Times are imminent, and only through suffering can they hope to win divine deliverance

Most Flagellants wander in large bands led by a Prophet of Doom who interprets Sigmar's will. They wear little more than rags, chains, and outlandish garments intended to cause discomfort and pain. Some follow armies, whipping themselves into a frenzy as battle is joined and fighting without thought for their own safety. Others
wrongs they must right. Good folk are expected to welcome, feed, and pray with Flagellants, though most fear and disdain them.

Flagellants eagerly join any group they believe will earn their god's favour, gladly taking penance upon themselves for the misdeeds of their companions. Playing a Flagellant means embracing unwavering faith and fanatical conviction. Your zeal may make you as much a challenge to your allies as to your enemies, but your fearless devotion and frenzied prowess in combat can prove invaluable.

**Note:** This profile reflects Sigmarite Flagellants, by far the most common in the Empire. If you want to play a self-punishing maniac dedicated to another god, give them the Lore Skill for their deity.
